hedge_knight: Sir Hedge drilled {scion} at the pell until her arms ached. "Again," he said, and again she struck.
{scion} came home with a split lip and a grin. "I nearly disarmed him, Father."
The old knight spoke little today, but watched her footwork with something close to approval.
hermit: The hermit set {scion} to copying psalms by candlelight, and corrected every crooked letter.
"Silence is also a prayer," the hermit told her. {scion} found it the hardest lesson yet.
{scion} returned smelling of woodsmoke and beeswax, her head full of saints' lives.
smuggler: The smuggler taught {scion} to weigh a coin by its ring on the table. She learned quickly. Too quickly, perhaps.
"Never look at the purse," the smuggler said. "Look at the hand that holds it."
{scion} haggled a fishwife down to half price, then felt a little guilty about it.

success: {scion} mucked out every stall and earned a nuzzle from the grey mare.
Hard work, honest pay. {scion} came home smelling of hay and horse.
The stablemaster grunted his thanks. From him, that is high praise.
A foal was born in the night, and {scion} was there to see it stand.
{scion} carried a dozen tankards at once and spilled not a drop.
The regulars sang her praises, and their tips were generous.
The alewife let {scion} keep the coins from a dice game she refereed fairly.
A drunken tinker tried to cheat the house. {scion} caught him at it.
failure: {scion} broke three cups and a stool. The alewife docked her wages.
A brawl broke out, and {scion} hid behind the barrels until it was over.
She mixed up the orders all night. Nobody was pleased.
A patron slipped away without paying, and the loss came out of her pay.

success: {scion} walked the walls till dawn and caught a pig thief red-handed.
The watch captain let {scion} carry the lantern at the head of the patrol.
A quiet night. {scion} kept her eyes open and the captain noticed.
{scion} talked two drunk ploughmen out of a fight before it started.
failure: {scion} fell asleep at her post. The captain was not amused.
A fox got into the hen coops on her watch. The farmers blamed the girl.
She chased a shadow into the mire and came home soaked and empty-handed.
The captain caught {scion} gossiping instead of watching the road.

success: {scion}'s lettering drew a nod from the Brother Librarian himself.
She finished a page of the psalter without a single blot.
{scion} found a misfiled charter, and the abbot was grateful.
The monks let {scion} grind the precious blue for the illuminators.
failure: {scion} knocked over an inkwell onto a fresh page. The Brother sighed deeply.
She dozed during vespers and was sent home early.
A misspelled saint's name cost her the day's wages.
{scion} smudged the gilding. Gold leaf is not cheap.

rest_home: {scion} slept late, then spent the afternoon mending by the hearth.
A quiet week. {scion} read aloud to {player} by candlelight.
Rain all week. {scion} watched it from the window and did nothing at all, gladly.
bathhouse: {scion} came home pink-cheeked and smelling of rosemary.
The bath-wife scrubbed {scion} raw and charged double for the soap.
Steam, gossip and hot stones. Her aching shoulders finally loosened.
shrine: {scion} lit a candle and sat in the cool dark until her thoughts stilled.
The old priest blessed her, then asked after {player}'s health.
She left a coin at the altar, and somehow felt lighter for it.
banquet: Roast swan, honeyed figs and minstrels. {scion} danced until the candles guttered.
{scion} ate too much marchpane and regretted none of it.
A lord's son asked {scion} to dance. She trod on his feet, twice.

idle: I wonder what lies beyond the hills...
Do I dream of fire because of the stories, or the other way round?
If I could be anything at all... what would I choose?
The swallows are back. Or are they leaving?
talk_ready: I have something on my mind...
